These properties are consistent with a transitional phase in which a hotter gaseous envelope partially exposes the central engine.

entries.title: A TESS Search for Optical Variability in Intermediate-mass Black Hole Candidates
entries.abstract: Optical variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) probes accretion onto black holes. We study the optical variability of AGNs in the mass range of intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, $10^{2-6}\,M_\odot$), whose expected variability damping timescales are of order days. We use the high-cadence photometry of the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to search for optical variability within its individual 28-day sectors. By applying the Quaver light-curve reduction pipeline and designing artifact-aware variability metrics, we identify 3 sources with high-confidence variability and 17 sources with medium-confidence variability. Fitting damped random walk (DRW) models reveals a tentative timescale-mass correlation in a small, metric-selected subset, but not in the full sample. ZTF difference-image aperture photometry reveals long-term fractional variability of 1.8-7.4% in the high-confidence sources, while most medium-confidence sources have variability below 1%. This study demonstrates that the dense cadence and repeated full-sky observations of TESS are valuable for detecting IMBH optical variability, while also being limited by its instrumental artifacts and relatively shallow field.

entries.title: An early interaction between the Sagittarius dwarf and the Milky Way I: Fossil signatures in the phase-space structure of the disc
entries.abstract: Several independent lines of evidence point to an early encounter between the Milky Way and the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy $5$-$7$ Gyr ago. We present four controlled $N$-body+hydro simulations, one of an isolated host galaxy and three of a single interaction between a Milky-Way-like host and a Sagittarius-like satellite on an unbound polar orbit. Relative to the fiducial satellite (with total mass $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$), one run increases the satellite's mass by a factor of $1.5$ and another its crossing speed by a factor of $1.4$, giving pericentric speeds of $466$-$634$ km s$^{-1}$ at pericentric radii of $R\simeq15$-$18$ kpc. Comparing the present-day, phase-space structure in radial bins by age of newly-formed thin-disc stars across the runs, we find that stars that existed at the time of the passage are thickened by up to $\sim37$ per cent in mass-enclosed height and heated by up to $\sim5$ km s$^{-1}$ in vertical velocity dispersion relative to the control, while stars formed after the passage are unaffected. The heating signature is also evident when comparing the age-vertical velocity dispersion relation against a heating relation with a power law of $0.38$, obtained by fitting the isolated host. A single, disc crossing from an early interaction thus suffices to leave lasting, datable fossils in the age-resolved vertical structure of a galactic disc. The fiducial run's dispersion jump of $\sim4$ km s$^{-1}$ matches best with that observed in the outer low-$α$ disc of the Milky Way (Das et al. 2024), corresponding to a perturber mass of $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$, with a velocity of $466$ km s$^{-1}$ at a pericentric radius of $16.7$ kpc, though the inversion from jump amplitude to perturber mass is good only to a factor of $\sim1.5$.

entries.title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
entries.abstract: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $λ$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $ε$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $ε$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $ε$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $ε$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $ε$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.

entries.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
entries.abstract: Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude ($A_g$), location ($W_{\rm g}^{\star}$), and width ($D_g$) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal{R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, $A_g$ shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal{R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of $A_g$ is concentrated in the large frequency separation range $Δν= 4.6$--$18.9\,μ$Hz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that $ν_{\rm max}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$ dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of $A_g$ reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution. Overall, for the synthetic grid adopted here, these results indicate that global properties provide a direct estimate of the buoyancy-glitch parameters and a way to prioritise dedicated mixed-mode inversions for large asteroseismic samples such as Kepler and PLATO.

entries.title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
entries.abstract: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.

analysis.result: For HSP blazars, soft X-ray polarimetry at $0.2-0.4\ \mathrm{keV}$ provides robust discrimination with predicted $\mathrm{PD} \approx 6.57\% - 8.38\%$ (e.g. Mrk 421 with $F_{0.2-0.4\,\mathrm{keV}} \approx 1.94 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ well above $\mathrm{MDP} = 1.19\%$), whereas leptonic models predict $\mathrm{PD} \approx 0\%$ in the MeV range ($0.2-5\ \mathrm{MeV}$, COSI) compared to $\approx 11\%$ in GOSoX. For LSP templates (BL Lac), $F_{0.2-0.4\,\mathrm{keV}} = 8.70_{-6.61}^{+6.61} \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ yields $\mathrm{PD} = 7.18_{-0.67}^{+0.49}\%$ with $\mathrm{MDP} = 3.09\%$ and an $89.2\%$ duty cycle.
analysis.problem: The high-energy emission mechanism in blazars is degenerate between leptonic models (SSC/EC with lower polarization) and hadronic models (proton synchrotron and cascades with higher polarization), while polarimetric observations below $1\ \mathrm{keV}$ remain completely unexplored.
analysis.method: Multi-wavelength SEDs are modeled with Bjet-MCMC and JetSeT for blazar templates (BL Lac, BZB J0211+1051, Mrk 501) across leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid models. analysis.reason: Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of massive white dwarfs in sculpted binary wind environments provides an attractive delayed formation channel for repeating FRBs in old stellar populations. Along non-polar sightlines ($\sim 94\%$), forward shocks cross the wind termination shock at $t_{\rm ts} \simeq 2.9\text{--}6.1\ \mathrm{yr}$, the shocked-wind contact discontinuity at $t_{\rm cw} \simeq 12\text{--}23\ \mathrm{yr}$, and the outer wind-bubble shock at $t_{\rm wb} \simeq 31\text{--}113\ \mathrm{yr}$. While unshocked ejecta dilute as ${\rm DM}_{\rm ejc} \propto t^{-2}$, shock ionization of upstream neutral circumstellar shells produces a sign reversal in $d{\rm DM}_{\rm loc}/dt$ from negative to positive at $t \simeq 9\text{--}22\ \mathrm{yr}$, reaching $+3\text{--}5\ \mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ in dense ambient clouds ($n_{\rm ext} = 500\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$). analysis.problem: What physical mechanisms drive the secular multi-year evolution and sign reversals of local dispersion measure (${\rm DM}_{\rm loc}$) observed in repeating fast radio bursts, particularly those situated in old stellar environments where long-delay formation pathways like accretion-induced collapse (AIC) operate within complex, pre-shaped circumstellar wind bubbles?
analysis.method: The authors develop an angle-dependent hydrodynamic model coupling aspherical homologous AIC ejecta ($M_{\rm ejc}, E_K$, prolate aspect ratio $\mathcal{A} = v_{\rm pol}/v_{\rm eq} = 1.5$, density power-law $\rho_{\rm ejc} \propto t^{n-3}r^{-n}$ with $n=10, \delta=0$) with a multi-zoned binary wind bubble ($t_w = 5000\ \mathrm{yr}$, $v_w = 1000\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, polar cavity $\theta_{\rm cav} = 20^\circ$). assumptions: The freely expanding AIC ejecta preserve total mass $M_{\rm ejc}$ and kinetic energy $E_K$ in a homologous self-similar profile before shock deceleration.

limits: The model neglects lateral pressure gradients, non-radial hydrodynamic mixing, and multidimensional fluid instabilities between adjacent angular cones.
